questions.question: How does the developer workflow fundamentally shift when transitioning from traditional edit-compile-debug loops to AI-augmented development?
options: Developers no longer need to write design specifications or document interfaces.
Developers replace manual testing entirely with automated model verifications.
Code compilation occurs automatically after every keystroke via remote inference servers.
The core routine shifts toward continuous speculative drafting and prompt refinement.
questions.explanation: AI-augmented workflows transform the traditional linear edit-compile-debug loop into continuous speculative drafting, where developers refine prompts and evaluate model suggestions iteratively.

questions.question: In the architecture of a modern AI code assistant, what is the primary role of the local IDE extension?
options: Compiling code and checking type correctness remote endpoints.
Executing deep learning model inference locally on client hardware.
Generating synthetic datasets for model fine-tuning.
Gathering telemetry, local buffers, and cursor position to pass to the orchestrator.
questions.explanation: The local IDE extension collects real-time editor state such as local buffer snippets, cursor position, and telemetry before handing them off to an orchestrator for prompt assembly.

questions.question: What primary trade-off occurs when expanding the context window scope to include more surrounding file content in autocompletion prompts?
options: Broader context increases generation latency while providing more accurate background.
Larger context budgets eliminate the possibility of model hallucinations.
A larger token budget speeds up model inference time.
Including open editor tabs automatically reduces memory usage on the client machine.
questions.explanation: Expanding the context scope gives the model useful ambient information, but processing more tokens increases prompt processing and overall inference latency.

questions.question: Which prompt contextualisation approach best ensures deterministic, correct code generation for a scoped task like a utility function?
options: Providing concise prompts without explicit type annotations to allow model flexibility.
Including entire workspace repositories to maximize context budget usage.
Relying on open-ended conversational requests without structural constraints.
Supplying explicit type signatures, interfaces, and minimal input-output examples.
questions.explanation: Explicit type signatures, explicit interface boundaries, and minimal examples constrain the generative search space without exhausting context token limits.

questions.question: Why might a developer choose a docked chat interface over passive inline ghost text when designing complex new logic?
options: Inline ghost text cannot generate multi-line completions.
Docked chat directly edits code buffers without developer approval.
Docked chat operates completely offline without inference latency.
Ghost text can create cognitive fatigue by continuously interrupting focus with immediate proposals.
questions.explanation: Inline ghost text can impose cognitive load and interrupt deep thought during complex architecture work, whereas conversational chat allows active, intentional elicitation when needed.

questions.question: During active development in an AI-assisted IDE, what happens to prompt payloads when a developer opens a relevant interface tab?
options: The model pauses all code completion until manual prompt submission.
The assistant purges all recent language server diagnostic logs.
The ambient context dynamically incorporates the new tab's interfaces into model prompts.
The IDE re-initializes the extension client entirely.
questions.explanation: Modern AI IDEs dynamically observe editor state changes, such as opening new tabs or importing interfaces via LSP, updating the prompt payload sent to the model in real time.

questions.question: A developer switches git branches to an older codebase, but the assistant suggests methods from an API introduced only in the newer branch. What issue is demonstrated here?
options: Over-contextualised prompt formatting.
Stale context carrying over across workspace environment state changes.
Context window token exhaustion.
Language Server Protocol diagnostic failure.
questions.explanation: Stale context occurs when an assistant retains cached snippets or file states from previous sessions or branches, causing suggestions that are invalid for the active workspace state.

questions.question: What combination of quality gates provides the most reliable guardrail before committing AI-assisted code to production?
options: Automated static analysis, local test suites, and strict human code review.
Restricting AI usage exclusively to writing documentation and docstrings.
Disabling all inline code completion tools during refactoring.
Solely relying on model self-verification prompts before rendering code.
questions.explanation: Automated linting and test suites catch immediate syntax and runtime errors, while human code review ensures overall logic correctness and prevents silent quality degradation.
